title: Persona Claim Types List — payload
description: Serve the claim-type registry this agent resolves against. A client that cannot read the table has to ship a copy of it, and a copy is a re-sync obligation on every change.

Response.title: Persona Claim Types List — response payload

registryVersion.description: Version of the core registry this agent implements — the version of _shared/claim-types.json, not of this task. A client caching the table keys the cache on this.

entries.description: The registered tokens. Both exact tokens and family prefixes appear here, undistinguished: which one an entry is follows from whether a given token equals it or descends from it, and marking them would invite a client to walk only one kind.

mask.description: Mask style, independent of sensitivity: any style that is not `none` is masked on screen whatever the sensitivity. Named rather than enumerated inline so a maintainer may serve a style this version does not list; a client that does not recognise a style MUST treat it as `full` rather than as `none`.

minimumSet.description: Marks a type a community may ask for without it being remarkable. The minimum set contains only normal-sensitivity, consent-release types; that is a rule rather than a coincidence.

oidc.description: OIDC standard claims this type answers. A recorded mapping, applied at presentation — the token stays the maintainer's own and no external vocabulary is primary.

unregistered.description: The floor: what a token with no entry and no registered prefix resolves to. Served rather than assumed, because a client that hard-codes it cannot be tightened by a maintainer that raises it.

strictness.description: Each axis ordered MOST PROTECTIVE FIRST. This is what makes rule 3 computable by a client: resolution takes the longest registered prefix and the unregistered floor and keeps whichever is more protective, which requires an ordering the client did not invent.
